title: Tokenizer + Chat-Template Fuzz Suite and Pin Validation Runbook
text:
Tokenizer + Chat-Template Fuzz Suite and Pin Validation Runbook

description:
Build and integrate a deterministic fuzz-testing suite and a pin-validation runner that exercises tokenizer and chat-template permutations during model onboarding. The goal is to catch tokenization drift, role-marker/escape regressions, and template alignment regressions early and to gate performance-profile publishing until a set of compatibility checks pass. Deliverables: (1) fuzz suite that generates edge-case prompts (control chars, long prefix/suffix, mixed encodings, RK/role escapes), (2) a pin-validation runner that verifies pinned model bundles against the golden template contract, (3) a runbook that maps failure classes to automated remediation or required engineer actions, (4) dashboards and alerts for gating failures prior to profile publish.

acceptance_criteria:
Fuzz suite integrated into onboarding CI and runs within 12m for nightly smoke
Pin-validation runner produces a pass/fail artifact with token-level diff and example repro prompts
Performance-profile publishing is prevented by a gating flag when compatibility failures are present
Coverage: role marker normalization, multibyte char splitting, KV-cache prefix preservation, template delimiter collision
On-failure runbook links to exact repro PR and a suggested mitigation (shim, template fallback, or pin update)

risks_and_tradeoffs:
Aggressive fuzz rules can produce false positives that block publishing. Conservative thresholds reduce noise but may miss subtle regressions. We will start with strict detection but soft-fail for non-blocking classes (label: informational) for two cycles, then tighten to block publishing after operator review. Running full corpus on every onboarding would increase CI cost; we will tier runs (fast smoke in CI, full corpus in nightly and pre-publish).

technical_notes:
- Implement generator that composes message envelopes varying role tokens, unicode sequences, and delimiter sequences.
- Token-diff output must include byte offsets and tokenizer variant used (bpe/byte-level, model-specific vocab fingerprint).
- Pin-validation runner will exercise pinned model bundle via local runtime shim; if runtime unavailable, fall back to a lightweight tokenizer-only check.
- Collect throughput and tokenization-time telemetry during runner to detect pathological cases that might skew performance profiles.

comments:
2026-03-05 Ava Chen: Created ticket after two onboarding regressions where chat templates shifted token counts (INC-2026-03). Decision: build a targeted fuzz harness rather than expanding existing unit tests.
2026-03-06 Mateo Ruiz: Spike notes uploaded to Confluence - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Fuzz+Spike. Found three classes of failures: delimiter collision, surrogate pair split, and role-escape duplication.
2026-03-08 Design review (Lina Ortiz): UX for repro artifacts proposed - include small visual token-diff and example chat transcript for Console release notes.
2026-03-09 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-runner/pull/214 - initial fuzz generator and runner harness. Status: draft.
2026-03-10 Engineering sync: Agreement to soft-block profile publishing only for 'token-count drift > 5%' and 'delimiter collision leading to role-loss'. Other classes informational initially.
2026-03-11 Mateo Ruiz: Integrated lightweight telemetry capture (latency per tokenize op) and added telemetry export to /dashboards/onboard/tokenizer-compat. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/onboard-tokenizer
2026-03-12 QA: Ran suite against 3 pinned nightly bundles. Results: one bundle failed delimiter collision test; added temporary template fallback in bundle metadata to avoid immediate outage. Created follow-up ENG-275002 to update fallback automation.
2026-03-13 Ava Chen: Runbook draft uploaded - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Tokenizer+Fuzz+Runbook. Includes mapping from failure code to remediation steps, owner assignments, and sample GitHub PR templates for fixes.
Next steps: tighten gating criteria after two successful dry-runs, add more corpus cases from customer telemetry, and add automated PR creation for simple fixes (e.g., normalize role markers).
